title: Vinsanto
subtitle: Santorini's sweet wine
objectives: Explain how Santorini Vinsanto is made
Compare it with Tuscan Vin Santo

steps.title: Sun-dried grapes
steps.body: Santorini's Vinsanto is a sweet wine made from at least 51% Assyrtiko, with Aidani. Grapes are picked late and dried in the sun for 12 to 14 days, concentrating sugar. The must ferments slowly, and the wine ages for at least two years in oak, often much longer.

steps.title: Ageing and taste
steps.body: Vinsanto can age 10, 20 or even 50 years in barrel, becoming deep amber to dark brown, with raisin, dried apricot, coffee, caramel and spice. Assyrtiko's acidity keeps it fresh despite very high sugar, often over 200 g/l. Its name may come from Santo, for Santorini, wine of Santorini.

steps.prompt: How are grapes for Santorini Vinsanto concentrated?
options: Dried in the sun for 12 to 14 days

steps.title: Not Tuscan Vin Santo
steps.body: Santorini's Vinsanto and Tuscany's Vin Santo share a name but differ. Tuscan Vin Santo uses Trebbiano and Malvasia dried indoors and ages in sealed caratelli. Santorini's uses Assyrtiko dried in the sun. The name's origin may link to Santorini or to holy wine, vino santo.

steps.prompt: Santorini Vinsanto and Tuscan Vin Santo use the same grapes.
steps.explanation: Not true. Santorini uses Assyrtiko and Aidani; Tuscany uses Trebbiano and Malvasia.

steps.title: What you learned
points: It ages for years, becoming amber with raisin and coffee
It differs from Tuscan Vin Santo in grapes and method
